_comment: GOVERNED CARRIER SHAPE — NOT a standalone event schema. This is the canonical Avro nested-record shape of a Movement (ADR-PC-032), the atom for moving money against one engine-owned account. It is NOT a `.avsc` (deliberately `.avsc.json`) because it is not an event: it is never catalogued, never registered under a Schema-Registry subject, and never published on its own. A money-moving event carries a list of these INSIDE its own payload — see usage below. The file extension keeps it out of the `*.avsc` glob the engine embeds (Babelstone.Engine.Avro.csproj), the catalog discovers (AvroSchemaCatalog), and the compat gate scans (scripts/avro-compat-check.sh).
_usage: A carrying event's .avsc declares a REQUIRED array field whose `items` is this record, inlined verbatim. Example field on a future LoanDisbursed: { "name": "movements", "type": { "type": "array", "items": <this record> } }. The engine's family-agnostic codec (MovementCarrier in AvroEventSerializer) binds the carrying event's IReadOnlyList<Movement> parameter to that array. An event with no movements carries an EMPTY array, never null.
_no_pii: account_ref is an OPAQUE reference the engine resolves internally, NEVER an IBAN / cleartext or ciphertext account identifier (ADR-PC-004 §P2). References are allowed on the durable bus; PII is not.
name: Movement
doc: One recorded change of value against a single engine-owned account (ADR-PC-032). Single-sided (one direction against one account_ref), family-agnostic, written append-first inside the money-moving event's payload. NOT a balanced double-entry pair — posting a balanced journal entry is the GL's job (ADR-PC-012), which the engine never does.

fields.name: account_ref
fields.doc: The legacy-Core / engine-owned account the value moves against — an OPAQUE token the engine resolves internally, NEVER an IBAN/cleartext or ciphertext PII identifier (ADR-PC-004 §P2). References are allowed on the bus; PII is not.

fields.name: direction
fields.doc: Debit | Credit, ALWAYS relative to account_ref: Debit = value leaves that account, Credit = value enters it (feature-design §2). Pinning direction to the named account resolves the 'a loan pays out yet was coded Debit' ambiguity. (SettlementDirection on the C# side.)

fields.name: amount_cents
fields.doc: The amount moved as integer EUR cents (Money.Cents, ADR-PC-010 §P1). The engine never expresses money as a float.

fields.name: value_date
fields.doc: The economic date the value moves (valid_time) as days since epoch — never wall-clock (ADR-PC-032 slot 1).

fields.name: operation
fields.doc: The CLOSED engine-side operation code naming WHICH money move this is (ADR-PC-032 slot 1, hardened to a closed type by feature-design §2) — an enum, NOT a free string. The settlement leg maps it to the ACL operation_type half of the idempotency key (ADR-IC-012 §P4). Family-agnostic generic verbs; each family chooses WHICH it carries, names none of its own. Widen forward-only by ADDING a symbol at the END (ADR-IC-002).

fields.name: origin
fields.doc: Who initiated the movement and what the spine does next (ADR-PC-032 slot 2). Originated = the decider decided it, so its cash leg is effected by the gated settlement leg. Observed = it arrived already cleared, so the engine only records it (no cash leg). v1 has no Observed producer (specified-but-dormant until shape 3).

fields.name: command_id
fields.doc: The ADR-PC-029 append-idempotency CommandId the originating command carried, threaded on for append idempotency + correlation (ADR-PC-032 slot 4). A replayed command id returns the original commit_sequence with no second append, so the movement is never double-written.
